items.title: Andaman junks two colonial-era laws with new prison regulation

File | Photo Credit: The Hindu The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have replaced two colonial-era prison laws with a new regulatory framework that provides for technology-driven administration and tighter security measures in jails.

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands Prisons and Correctional Services Regulation, 2026, published by the Union Law Ministry on Tuesday (November 18, 2026), repealed the Prisons Act, 1894, the Prisoners Act, 1900, and the Transfer of Prisoners Act, 1950.

The Regulation, comprising 70 Sections across 14 Chapters, provides for six categories of prisons — district prisons, sub-prisons, open institutions, high-security prisons, women's prisons and young offender institutions.
The new law mandates the use of biometric identification, CCTV surveillance, computerised prison records linked to the Interoperable Criminal Justice System and mobile jammers.

items.title: Karnataka government replaces single-commissioner system governing Bengaluru police
points: The Karnataka government on Wednesday replaced the single-commissioner system governing Bengaluru police and appointed four Indian Police Service officers to head separate divisions under a chief commissioner.
Additional director general R Hithendra will be the chief commissioner, and Labhu Ram, P S Harsha, Vikash Kumar Vikash and M B Boraligaiah commissioners for Central, East, West and North Bengaluru.
Hithendra takes over from Seemanth Kumar Singh, who has been named Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Services additional director general.

The previous commissionerate covered a jurisdiction of approximately 1,294 sq km and a population of about 15.6 million.
The state Cabinet approved the five-commissionerate model on October 6.

China, Korea and Japan accounted for about 93 percent of global shipbuilding in 2024, according to Clarksons Research, and India is spending public money to become the fourth name on that list, with Korean partners instead of Chinese ones.
About 95 percent of India’s trade by volume moves by sea, the country spends close to $75 billion a year hiring foreign ships, and its own yards held 0.5 percent of the global order book as of Sept.

items.title: API crude stock report shows lower-than-expected inventory build
points: The American Petroleum Institute (API) released its latest report on U.S. crude oil inventories, revealing a significant development in the oil market.
The report indicated that crude stockpiles increased by 5.3 million barrels.
This figure fell short of market expectations, which had anticipated a more substantial build-up in inventories.
The actual increase of 5.3 million barrels is notably lower than the previous report, which recorded a significant rise of 9 million barrels.
The lower-than-expected increase in crude inventories implies a stronger demand for oil than analysts had forecasted, which could have bullish implications for crude prices.

items.title: One in five refineries at closure risk as global oil demand peaks in 2032
points: An estimated one in five of the world’s oil refineries faces increasing risk of closure as global oil demand peaks and enters structural decline within the next decade, according to new research published today by Wood Mackenzie.
Global refined product demand stands at 105 million barrels per day.
Wood Mackenzie forecasts a rise to 108 mb/d by 2032, after which decline sets in.
Roughly 20% of existing global capacity sits on what the report terms a “downward escalator,” facing falling or negative operating net cash margins and increasing risk of closure.
Demand peaks in 2032, but with 2040 only three to four refinery turnaround cycles away, the window for major investment decisions is closing.

“The sector has navigated structural change before, from the oil shocks of the 1970s to the investment capacity wave across the Middle East and Asia in the 2000s,” said Alan Gelder, SVP Refining, Chemicals and Oil Markets, Wood Mackenzie.

points: European natural gas prices held their recent advance above €85/MWh on Wednesday, as traders weighed persistent tensions in the Middle East and Europe’s winter supply outlook.

Usually, a potentiometer in a PS5 or Xbox controller can survive for thousands of cycles without wear and tear from friction, but due to excessive dust, hair, or gunk, they get more resistance and interferes with sensor contacts, thus causing stick drift.

items.title: India considers 50% cut in STT on stocks, higher tax on derivatives
points: Indian revenue officials are reviewing proposals to increase taxes on stock derivatives while reducing the securities transaction tax on share trading by 50 per cent.
The proposals include a 50% reduction in the securities transaction tax on buying and selling of stocks, one of the people said.
Equity derivatives account for 227-times the turnover in Indian cash markets, compared with four-times in the US and 29-times in Germany.

Nearly 88% of individual traders in equity derivatives lost money in the year through March 2026, according to the Securities and Exchange Board of India, with their combined net losses totaling about 917 billion rupees ($10 billion).
Options accounted for 92% of those losses.
Long-term gains on listed equities held for more than a year are taxed at 12.5%, while short-term gains attract a 20% levy.
In February 2026 budget, the government increased STT on equity futures to 0.05% from 0.02%.
The tax on options premium, as well as the exercise of options, was increased to 0.15%.

items.title: No Insurance? Crossing A Toll Plaza Will Get You A Rs 10,000 Fine
points: According to a report that surfaced online in August this year, around 56 percent of the vehicles plying on our roads are uninsured.
The Supreme Court had also asked insurance regulators and other concerned authorities to take action and come up with a plan to reduce the numbers.
The National Highways Authority, as part of the plan, has now started a pilot project where it aims to identify vehicles on the road without valid insurance.
Under this new project, a vehicle without a valid insurance policy can receive a fine of up to Rs 10,000.
The pilot project has been launched at Mundka toll plaza on Delhi’s Urban Extension Road-II.

items.title: VB-G RAM G would have raised states’ burden over six-fold in 2025-6: PRS report

Under MGNREGA, the Centre paid the entire wage cost and 75% of material costs, while states bore the remaining material expenditure and administrative costs beyond the Centre’s contribution.

Under the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), or VB-G RAM G—which replaced MGNREGA from July 1, 2026—states bear 40% of the wage, material, and administrative expenditure, while the Centre contributes 60%.
